# ROI of automated dispute intake (generated by `python -m src.eda.roi` — do not edit)

**What this is.** An estimate of what the agent saves if it takes the dispute-intake contacts that LATAM Bank's call center handles today. Contact volumes, handling times and satisfaction come from the dataset; automation rate, unsafe rate and LLM cost come from the held-out evaluation of the deployed configuration. The dataset is synthetic and near-uniform in places (see `eda_findings.md` Q12), so read the result as a method with order-of-magnitude numbers, not a forecast.

## Inputs from the data

| input | value | source |
|---|---|---|
| Complaint contacts in 2025 | 39,217 | `call_center_interactions`, reason = Queja |
| Share of complaints that are disputes (unrecognized charge + undue fee) | 36.3% | `complaints` 2025 |
| → estimated dispute contacts per year | **14,238** | contacts × share (assumes contacts mirror the complaint mix) |
| Median handling time of a complaint contact | 431 s | `duration_seconds` |
| Average customer wait before an agent | 120 s | `wait_time_seconds` |
| First-contact resolution / follow-up needed | 43.6% / 63.0% | `was_resolved`, `requires_followup` |
| Interactions per agent per month | 454 | `service_agents` (active) |
| CSAT (1–4) when the complaint contact is resolved vs not | 3.00 vs 2.00 | `satisfaction_surveys` × interactions |
| Dispute complaints: median days to first response / to resolution, SLA breached | 1.5 d / 15 d, 20.2% | `complaints` |

## Inputs from the evaluation (deployed hybrid, 230 sealed conversations)

| input | value |
|---|---|
| Conversations fully handled with no transfer and a correct outcome | 67.0% |
| Unsafe outcomes | 0 / 230 |
| LLM cost per automated resolution | $0.0006 |

The evaluation mix over-weights hard cases on purpose (74 of 230 must be escalated), so the real containment of ordinary dispute traffic is likely higher; the table below varies it.

## Savings per year

| containment | contacts automated | agent hours saved | agent FTE freed | customer wait saved (h) | net USD saved @ $6/h | net USD saved @ $10/h | net USD saved @ $15/h |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 40% | 5,695 | 682 | 1.0 | 190 | 3,488 | 6,215 | 9,624 |
| 55% | 7,831 | 938 | 1.4 | 261 | 5,021 | 8,771 | 13,459 |
| 67% (eval) | 9,533 | 1,141 | 1.8 | 318 | 6,243 | 10,808 | 16,515 |

## Cost per resolution

| | cost per contact |
|---|---|
| Human agent (median 431 s) | $0.72 / $1.20 / $1.80 at $6 / $10 / $15 per hour |
| Agent: LLM | $0.0006 |
| Agent: infrastructure ($50/month over the eval-containment volume) | $0.063 |

**Per contact the agent costs about 5% of a human-handled contact at $10/h.** This ratio does not depend on the bank's size; the absolute savings above do, and this synthetic bank is small (about 39k complaint contacts a year).

## What it does not claim

- The agent automates **intake**: identity, finding the charge, filing a verified dispute, blocking the card. Investigating the dispute still takes the bank's process (median 15 days today); the agent removes the 1.5-day wait for a first response on the intake step, not the investigation.
- Satisfaction: resolved complaint contacts score 3.0 vs 2.0 for unresolved ones (CSAT 1–4). Only 44% are resolved on first contact today; the evaluation suggests the agent resolves in-scope intake in one conversation, but no CSAT was measured on the agent itself.
- Costs exclude building and maintaining the system, and the human time spent on the cases it escalates (those already reach an agent today, with everything verified, so handling should be shorter, but that is not measured).
- Agent cost per hour and infrastructure cost are assumptions, shown as scenarios.
